title: 5. Leading Operational KPIs, Structural Potential & CEO Walk-the-Talk

epigraph.quote: In biopharma, management credibility is not measured by the boldness of a 10-year revenue target; it is measured by clinical trial hit rates, gross-to-net honesty, and operating-margin discipline.
epigraph.author: Institutional Capital Allocation Audit

web_blocks.html: Tracking Gilead's business means looking past noisy GAAP EPS swings caused by acquired IPR&D charges. Instead, investors should watch six core operating KPIs that drive long-term cash flow [1, 4]. These are: (1) Biktarvy U.S. HIV share; (2) Yeztugo launch pace and total PrEP sales; (3) Trodelvy first-line mTNBC uptake; (4) Kite cell-therapy volume and anito-cel approval; (5) Livdelzi PBC share gains; and (6) R&D, deal spending, and non-GAAP margin control [1, 4].

web_blocks.takeaway: Five of six commercial KPIs are firing in 2026 (led by Yeztugo, Biktarvy, Trodelvy, and Livdelzi), while Kite's core cell-therapy erosion and $12.4B of 2026 acquired IPR&D keep capital-allocation discipline on watch.

web_blocks.html: CEO Walk-the-Talk Audit (Daniel O'Day & CFO Andrew Dickinson, 2019–2026): When Daniel O'Day became CEO in March 2019, he made three clear multi-year pledges. First, he aimed to grow cancer drugs to one-third of Gilead's sales by 2030. Second, he pledged to extend HIV leadership past Biktarvy using long-acting capsid science. Third, he promised tight core cost control while funding new drugs. Seven years later, his report card splits sharply between virology execution (A) and cancer M&A execution (C+). Investors should judge management by cash results and trial hit rates rather than long-range slogans.

On the positive side, O'Day and medical chiefs Merdad Parsey and Dietmar Berger delivered a major win with lenacapavir. PURPOSE-1 and PURPOSE-2 showed ~100% HIV prevention efficacy. Yeztugo won FDA approval in June 2025 and scaled to a ~$1 billion run rate in 2026 [4, 5]. Management also raised full-year 2026 base-business sales guidance by $1.6 billion over the year [4]. In addition, buying CymaBay for $4.3 billion after Phase 3 success proved far wiser than 2020's early-stage bets, yielding a fast winner in Livdelzi [11]. CFO Andy Dickinson has also kept non-GAAP R&D and SG&A growth low while launching Yeztugo, Livdelzi, and 1L Trodelvy at the same time [3, 4].

On the negative side, O'Day's 2019 goal—making cancer one-third (~33%) of total sales by 2030—remains behind schedule. In FY2025, cancer and cell therapy brought in ~$3.2 billion, or 11% of total sales [3]. Even with Trodelvy up 42% in Q3 2026, Kite's mid-teens drop keeps total cancer near 11%–12% of the $31 billion sales base [4]. Reaching 25%–33% by 2030 now hinges on anito-cel winning FDA approval on December 23, 2026 [10]. It must also take real share from Carvykti without repeating past write-offs like Forty Seven ($4.9 billion) or Trodelvy ($2.4 billion in 2024) [19].

web_blocks.title: Structural Potential: What Happens If Anito-cel & Weekly Oral Lenacapavir Both Hit?
paragraphs: Between December 2026 and February 2027, Gilead faces two big FDA decisions. Anito-cel has a PDUFA date on December 23, 2026, and weekly oral lenacapavir has a PDUFA date on February 2, 2027. Both test Gilead's 2028–2035 earnings bridge. If both win approval, anito-cel can refill Kite's cleanrooms while oral lenacapavir expands PrEP reach. Together, they give Gilead a solid path to absorb the ~$1.5B Biktarvy IRA cut in 2028 without shrinking cash flow.

book_paragraphs: When you and I audit a management team over a five-to-seven-year stretch, we don't grade them on their slide decks; we grade them on whether the promises they made in Year One showed up in the cash register by Year Seven. Daniel O'Day arrived at Gilead from Roche in March 2019 with three clear promises: first, turn oncology into one-third of Gilead's revenue by 2030; second, protect and extend the HIV franchise past Biktarvy; and third, keep core operating expenses disciplined so cash flow keeps funding the dividend.

Let's grade all three honestly as of November 2026. On HIV, O'Day gets an A. Lenacapavir—branded Yeztugo—is a genuine scientific breakthrough. Delivering 100% protection in PURPOSE-1 and scaling to a $1 billion annualized run rate in its first full year on the market is textbook commercial execution, and settling Biktarvy's U.S. patent litigation out to April 2036 bought the company an extra two-plus years of runway. On cost discipline, CFO Andy Dickinson also earns high marks: base-business revenue is growing 16% in Q3 2026 while core R&D and SG&A have barely budged.

On the oncology target, however, the scorecard is much more sobering. Seven years after O'Day set the one-third-of-revenue-by-2030 goal, oncology sits at roughly 11% to 12% of total sales—around $3.2 billion in 2025—despite $45 billion-plus of cumulative oncology and cell-therapy M&A across Kite, Forty Seven, Immunomedics, and now Arcellx. Trodelvy's June 2026 first-line breast cancer approval finally put wind in its sails, yet Kite's core lymphoma franchise is shrinking mid-teens in 2026.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: The shift in Gilead's deal-making style between 2020 and 2024–2026 is encouraging: Forty Seven was bought on early Phase 1b data and blew up; CymaBay was bought after Phase 3 success and became a 93%-growth winner. Arcellx sits in between—Phase 2 iMMagine-1 data are compelling, but we won't know if $7.8 billion was disciplined until anito-cel clears its December 23, 2026 PDUFA and competes head-to-head with Carvykti.

book_subsections.title: The Six Operational Gauges on Our Dashboard
paragraphs: If you want to track Gilead over the next eight quarters without getting distracted by GAAP noise, keep your eyes on six operational gauges. Gauge one is Biktarvy's U.S. share, now at an all-time high of 53%. Gauge two is Yeztugo's quarterly sequential ramp—$305 million in Q3 2026, up 31% from Q2—and whether the once-weekly oral tablet wins approval on February 2, 2027.

Gauge three is Trodelvy's first-line triple-negative breast cancer uptake, which jumped 42% to $506 million in Q3 2026. Gauge four is Kite's cell-therapy stabilization and anito-cel's December 23, 2026 FDA decision. Gauge five is Livdelzi's march toward $1 billion in PBC after hitting $203 million in Q3 2026. And gauge six is M&A restraint: after committing $12.4 billion to acquired IPR&D in 2026, shareholders need a pause on mega-deals so free cash flow can pay down debt.
